conventions.signature_encoding: Wire-sourced signing fields are base64url: b64u64 = 86 chars for 64 bytes. This includes `presented_*`/`pinned_identity_binding_signature` (I1-I3), `envelope_json.prekey.signature` (F1/M2/M3), `signed_prekey.signature` (B3) and `prekey.signature` (B4), i.e. `B3.expected.signature` and `B4.expected.signature` ARE wire values and MUST be b64u64. A wire-valid vector MUST NOT carry 128 hex chars in those fields. Internal byte-level KAT values are kept separately as `*_hex` (A2.expected.signature, B3/B4.expected.signature_hex, B5.expected.*_identity_binding_signature, meta.public_keys.*_identity_binding_signature) and never appear on the wire.

meta.warning: All private keys below are public test material. Never use them outside tests.
meta.supersedes: vector_set_version 3 (43 vectors, 273 checks). Envelope wire format is unchanged (envelope.v=1, header.v=1, AD 163 B). B3/B4 `signature` fields were re-encoded from internal hex to the canonical wire b64u64 (same 64 bytes; hex kept as `signature_hex`), G2/G3 notes correct the safety-number entry size (64 B, not 80), L1 gained `failed_chain_dh` (P1-C window anchor) with recomputed framing, and M3 + L3b were added (P1-B-1, P1-C-1).

limits.arithmetic_note: 512 KiB is the WIRE (HTTP body) limit; the old §4.7 compared 512 KiB against the DECODED sum, which would allow ~683 KiB on the wire. 9 canonical envelopes = 396 KiB wire; 10 = 440 KiB. Per-envelope form cap 65536 encoded chars is NOT a fan-out budget: 10 x 65536 chars > 512 KiB. S4: the DB CHECK accepts only the canonical 33040 decoded bytes; the 65536 encoded-char form guard rejects oversized input before base64-decode and is not a delivery promise.

normative_invariants.direct_key: Every type='DIRECT' chat has direct_key = least(A,B)::text||':'||greatest(A,B)::text over the SET of distinct chat_members.user_id, independent of member status (REMOVED/INVITED are still pair members). A DIRECT chat with != 2 distinct member rows is corrupt and the migration must stop with DIRECT_KEY_UNRESOLVED; a duplicate live pair stops it with DIRECT_PAIR_DUPLICATE. CHECKs are added NOT VALID and validated after backfill.
normative_invariants.envelope_coverage: peer_devices, self_devices, peer_covered and self_covered count ONLY devices with e2ee_capable=true (identity_key_alg='Ed25519+X25519', ACTIVE). An envelope addressed to a non-capable device is rejected 422 E2EE_LEGACY_DEVICE before Message/seq; a legacy device is never a candidate, never coverage, and never appears in uncovered_device_ids.
normative_invariants.reset_retry_window: SESSION_RESET carries failed_session_id, failed_chain_dh, failed_n, reason and retry_of_client_message_id. The sender re-encrypts only messages at/after retry_of_client_message_id in local send order (per-session), each with a new client_message_id and retry_of_client_message_id in the inner payload; the receiver discards a re-sent message whose retry_of_client_message_id it already decrypted.
normative_invariants.ciphertext_cap: Accepted E2EE ciphertext is canonical v1: decoded 16..33040 bytes (33024 padded + 16 tag) = at most 44054 b64u chars. The DB CHECK stores only canonical values; the API's 65536 encoded-char form guard is a pre-decode DoS bound, not a delivery promise. Anything above the canonical cap is 413 ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE (details.reason='canonical').
normative_invariants.claim_workspace: auth.claim_one_time_prekey requires the chat to belong to ops.current_workspace_id() and the caller to be an ACTIVE member; a chat from another workspace yields UNKNOWN_DEVICE.
normative_invariants.verification_ownership: auth.key_verifications enforces verifier ownership with a composite FK (verifier_user_id, verifier_device_id) -> auth.devices(user_id, id) and FKs to chat/chat.chats/devices; a BEFORE INSERT trigger requires verifier and target to be ACTIVE members of the same chat in the current (non-deleted) workspace, while RLS stays a tenant boundary so revoke/soft-delete can still update revoked_at.

vectors.source: NIST CAVP gcmEncryptExtIV256, PT len 0 / AAD len 0, 96-bit IV, zero key

expected.note: AES-GCM output = ciphertext || 16-byte tag; empty plaintext yields tag only

sections.title: X3DH handshake (4-DH with one-time prekey, and 3-DH fallback)

vectors.note: No one-time prekey: DH4 omitted; IKM = F || DH1 || DH2 || DH3. Weaker forward secrecy; client must warn.

Signed prekey signature created by the device identity signing key at POST /devices. P2-6: `expected.signature` is the canonical WIRE value of `signed_prekey.signature` (base64url, 86 chars, 64 bytes); the byte-level KAT value is in `expected.signature_hex` and never appears on the wire.

Signed X3DH initial-message preamble. Binding: chat, both devices, both identities (signing + DH), all prekey material, session id. P2-6: `expected.signature` is the canonical WIRE value of `prekey.signature` (base64url, 86 chars, 64 bytes); the byte-level KAT value is in `expected.signature_hex` and never appears on the wire.

Self-signature binding IK_sig -> IK_dh (P1-2). Signed message = D_IKBIND || u8(1) || IK_dh_pub || IK_sig_pub (88 bytes). POST /devices stores it; the server verifies it; the client MUST re-verify it on every claim and on every key change, before trusting the bundle or updating the TOFU pin.

sections.title: HKDF and Double Ratchet KDF chains

vectors.note: RatchetInitAlice: RK1||CKs = HKDF(ikm=DH(A0, SPK_B), salt=SK, info=dr-root, L=64).
KDF_CK: mk = HMAC-SHA256(ck, 0x01); ck' = HMAC-SHA256(ck, 0x02).

sections.title: AEAD encryption, plaintext framing, padding and associated data

vectors.note: raw = domain||u8(1)||u8(1=TEXT_JSON)||u32be(len(body))||body; zero-pad to multiple of 256.
First message of the session (prekey envelope). AD is the 163-byte structure from §3.2.
Second message in the same sending chain, n=1, no prekey block.

sections.title: Full Double Ratchet conversation (4 messages, 2 DH ratchet turns)

vectors.note: Alice initiates with the prekey envelope (m1). Bob's initial ratchet private key is the signed prekey. After m1 Bob performs the first DH ratchet and replies with a fresh ratchet key. Counters: pn = messages sent in previous sending chain, n = index in current chain.

initial_state.note_ratchet_derivation: Both sides: RK_1||CK = HKDF(ikm=DH(ratchet, peer ratchet pub), salt=SK, info=dr-root, L=64).

sections.title: Out-of-order delivery and skipped message keys

vectors.note: Post-handshake chain (no prekey). Receiver gets m1 (n=0), then m3 (n=2): it MUST derive and store the key for n=1, decrypt m3, and later decrypt m2 from the stored key. Duplicate n must be rejected; gap > MAX_SKIP (1000) must be rejected.
Wire object exactly as sent inside POST /messages envelopes[]. b64url values are unpadded. JSON text is illustrative; field values are normative.
No prekey block: flags bit0 = 0, preamble_hash = 32 zero bytes. Same session and chain (n=0 after ratchet).

sections.title: Fingerprints, safety number and verification metadata

vectors.note: FP = SHA-256(domain || IK_sig_pub || IK_dh_pub). 32 bytes.
Per device pair: two 64-byte entries (user_id(16)||device_id(16)||fingerprint(32)), sorted lexicographically; SHA-512; decimal mod 10^60, zero-padded; displayed as 12 groups of 5.
Bob's device re-registered with a new identity signing key: digits MUST change; the old verification is invalid.

VH v2 (P0-1): the verifier's DEVICE is part of the hash. VH = SHA-256(D_VER || u8(2) || chat_id(16) || verifier_user_id(16) || verifier_device_id(16) || target_device_id(16) || u32(target_key_generation) || ascii(digits_60)). Rows created with u8(1) MUST be treated as unverified (migration: verifier_device_id IS NULL).

P0-1 regression: Alice has two devices (L1=...011, L2=...012). L1 verified Bob in this chat; L2 never did. The device-pair safety numbers differ (L2 has a different fingerprint/device_id), VH v2 binds the verifier device, and GET /chats/{id}/keys returned to L2 MUST report verified=null for Bob. A server-side boolean keyed only by user is a defect.

sections.title: Sender key chain (INFORMATIVE — groups are out of E7 scope, ADR-05)

vectors.note: NOT part of E7 acceptance. Same KDF_CK as DR; per-epoch chain; no PCS across epochs. Included so E7 vectors do not need revision when groups start.
AD for sender-key messages (informative): domain||v||chat_id||sender_device_id||epoch||n. No recipient device id (one ciphertext for all).

sections.title: TOFU pinning of the sender identity per device_id (P0-2, negative test)

vectors.note: First contact: no pin for sender_device_id. The recipient verifies the preamble signature, then the IK_sig->IK_dh binding, then records the TOFU pin BEFORE showing the message. Acceptance is honest but the device is UNVERIFIED; the safety number must be compared out-of-band. This vector also demonstrates the residual TOFU window: keys substituted at first contact are not detected by pinning. P1-E: presented/pinned binding signatures are wire base64url (b64u64, 86 chars), not hex; a conforming client must parse them before TOFU.

expected.residual_risk: TOFU window: attacker present at first contact is not detected by pinning

vectors.note: P0-2 negative: the server substitutes the identity pair for an EXISTING device_id. The prekey envelope is wire-valid, the preamble signature verifies (Mallory's own keys), recipient keys/session_id/AD/AEAD all pass. Only the local pin (device_id -> IK_sig/IK_dh/fingerprint) detects the substitution. MUST be KEY_CHANGE_DETECTED: do not create/overwrite the session, do not display, do not consume the OPK, block sending until explicit user confirmation. P1-E: all signature fields are wire b64u64; the 64-byte binding is decoded, not hex-parsed.

P0-2b negative: stolen bearer token without device private keys. The prekey block carries Mallory's IK_sig/IK_dh and EK for the EXISTING sender_device_id 011; the preamble signature verifies and Mallory's IK_sig->IK_dh binding is valid, but those keys are NOT the keys registered in auth.devices and NOT the keys in the claim bundle / GET /chats/{id}/keys. The server MUST reject 422 INVALID_ENVELOPE_FORMAT (409 KEY_CHANGED if generation moved); the recipient MUST reject KEY_HANDSHAKE_INVALID before creating a session, consuming the OPK or displaying the message. Binding verification alone is insufficient: it only proves that the presented IK_sig owns the presented IK_dh, not that the pair belongs to device_id 011. This is the exact gap that P0-2b closes; it is wire-valid and byte-identical to I1's envelope.

inputs.attacker_capability: stolen bearer token only; no device private keys

expected.test: integration: device A with a bearer token but without its private keys cannot establish a prekey session as A

sections.title: security_mode immutability and downgrade resistance (P0-3, P1-12)

vectors.note: A downgrade of an existing E2EE chat is an attack, not configuration. Server: immutable column + trigger (409 MODE_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN), no API to change the mode. Client: pins chat_id -> security_mode; if the server reports MANAGED for a pinned E2EE chat, it MUST NOT send plaintext and MUST show a security alert. Switching modes requires a NEW chat.

P1-12: with e2ee.enabled=false the server MUST NOT create E2EE workspaces/chats and MUST NOT show the E2EE badge. Existing E2EE chats, if any, remain E2EE and MUST NOT accept plaintext; the flag only gates NEW E2EE surfaces.

P1-G: a new device or a cleared profile has no local chat_id->security_mode pin. A malicious/compromised server may answer MANAGED for a chat that has E2EE history and a peer with e2ee_capable devices. The client MUST NOT silently send plaintext: it blocks before any request, shows a security alert and requires an explicit mode decision / E2EE session. There is no server-side code for this case: a server that really says MANAGED would accept plaintext, so the control is client-side only. Honest residual risk: without a local pin and without server-signed mode attestation (v2) the client cannot prove the chat was E2EE.

expected.allow_after_user_confirmation: E2EE_ONLY (or a NEW managed chat; never an in-place downgrade)
expected.residual_risk: no local pin and no server-signed mode attestation v1; the client cannot prove the chat was E2EE

sections.title: client_message_id uniqueness scope and cross-user replay (P1-10, D-07)

vectors.note: Scope is (chat_id, sender_id, client_message_id). A repeat by the SAME sender with the same body is an idempotent replay (same id/seq). The value MUST be echoed in Message and MUST NOT be included in AD.

A different sender using the same UUID in the same chat MUST NOT receive the first user's message as a replay. The lookup is sender-scoped; otherwise a 201 replay leaks another user's message. Expected: 409 CLIENT_MESSAGE_ID_CONFLICT.

R-15 control payload: content_type=2 (SESSION_RESET) inside a NEW prekey envelope; not user-visible, no notification, not counted as a user message. S4 (P1-C): the body carries `failed_chain_dh` = header.dh of the failed message and `failed_n` = its header.n; together with `retry_of_client_message_id` they define the exact retry window (L3b). Unauthenticated WS events are NOT used for reset (spoofable).

R-15 mitigation: the receiver never silently drops; it emits an encrypted reset signal, rate-limited to one per failed session, and the sender performs exactly one new prekey handshake. The retry is a NEW message with a NEW client_message_id (the old id already points at the old ciphertext); UI replaces the local pending copy, not duplicates it.

P1-C: reset is a property of the failed SESSION, not of one message. A sent m1..m5 in one session; B was offline past the SPK window and decrypted none. One SESSION_RESET for that failed_session_id makes A re-encrypt ALL undelivered messages of the session into a new session, each with a NEW client_message_id/Idempotency-Key, in order, replacing the local pending copies (one retry group, no duplicates). Batch is capped at 20; the rest stay retry_pending with an explicit UI status. Empty outbox is a no-op (no new handshake).

P1-C-1: L3 covers the case where NOTHING was delivered (delivered_before_reset=0) and the whole session is re-encrypted. The dangerous case is partial delivery: B decrypted m1..m3 and failed on m4. Re-encrypting all five would duplicate m1..m3 in B's UI with brand-new client_message_ids (no way to correlate). S4 rule: the reset carries `failed_chain_dh` + `failed_n` (header.dh/header.n of the first message that failed) and `retry_of_client_message_id`; A re-encrypts only messages from that anchor onward in local send order (m4, m5), each with a NEW client_message_id AND `retry_of_client_message_id` inside the inner payload. Second line of defence: if a re-encrypted message points at a `retry_of_client_message_id` the receiver already decrypted, the receiver discards it silently (no UI duplicate, no unread, no notification) - this also covers a sender window bug. Both mechanisms are covered below; nothing is silently lost.

inputs.retry_window_rule: local_send_index >= index(retry_of_client_message_id); chain/n are the wire labels

duplicate_guard_case.why: sender window bug: m3 (already decrypted) is re-sent as well

sections.title: Peer coverage: candidates vs covered devices (P1-B)

vectors.note: P1-B: peer_devices>0 but peer_covered==0. This happens when the recipient has capable devices but no usable SPK/bundle, so the sender only has a self-envelope or self-fan-out. The server MUST reject 409 E2EE_NO_PEER_ENVELOPE before creating the Message/seq; a 201 with no peer delivery is a silent loss. The client must also pre-check and not send when no peer bundle was obtained.

expected.retry_after: peer has an active SPK / a peer bundle is available

vectors.note: P1-B: one of two peer devices is covered. The message is accepted (at least one peer envelope exists) but the response MUST carry warning=PEER_DEVICE_UNCOVERED and list the uncovered device; the UI says the message is unavailable on some of the peer's devices. The envelope is the wire-valid F1 prekey envelope addressed to Bob's device 021; Bob's second device 022 has no envelope.

expected.ui: unavailable on some of the peer's devices

vectors.note: P1-B-1: coverage counts ONLY e2ee_capable devices. Bob has B1=...021 (capable) and B2=...023 (legacy ACTIVE, no keys, e2ee_capable=false). A crafted envelope addressed to the legacy device must be rejected 422 E2EE_LEGACY_DEVICE during per-envelope target validation, before Message/seq (no partial fan-out). Even if that gate were skipped, peer_covered would remain 0 because the legacy device is not capable -> 409 E2EE_NO_PEER_ENVELOPE. peer_devices (candidates) = 1 (capable only); the legacy device is not a candidate and is not listed in uncovered_device_ids (it is not a delivery target at all). Variant B (capable-only envelope) is accepted with peer_covered=1=peer_devices and warning=null, so the legacy device can never produce false coverage or a false warning. The embedded envelope is shape-valid v1 (no prekey: a legacy device has no SPK, so no real session can exist with it); the server rejects it on capability, not on crypto.

inputs.coverage_counting_rule: distinct recipient_device_id where device.e2ee_capable AND device.user_id = peer_user_id

expected.ui: legacy devices are not addressed by E2EE at all; no 'unavailable on some devices' warning

sections.title: Device registration: revoked idempotency and legacy addressability (P1-6/P2-4/P2-5)

vectors.note: P2-5: replaying the same IK pair after the device was REVOKED must not resurrect it. The REVOKED check runs BEFORE identity-key idempotency: 410 DEVICE_REVOKED, no reactivation, no new device row with the same keys. To participate in E2EE again the client registers a NEW device with a NEW identity pair (the global unique index excludes REVOKED, but the server still refuses to reuse tombstoned keys).

P2-4: E2EE_LEGACY_DEVICE must be reachable. POST /devices cannot address an existing legacy device (no device_id in the body), so the code is returned by POST /devices/{deviceId}/prekeys for a legacy target: 422 E2EE_LEGACY_DEVICE with details.remedy=register_new_device. Claim still reports such a device as unavailable[reason=NO_KEYS]; the two codes have disjoint scopes.

sections.title: Plaintext fields in E2EE: reply_to_id and server-forged text (P1-F/P2-13)

vectors.note: P1-F: reply_to_id is allowed ONLY inside the encrypted inner payload. A top-level reply_to_id in MessageCreate for an E2EE chat leaks plaintext metadata and is rejected 422 E2EE_PLAINTEXT_FORBIDDEN (details.field=reply_to_id) before Message/seq creation; the DB CHECK ck_messages_e2ee_no_reply_to_id is the second line. reply_to_id is NOT part of AD and does not change the envelope wire format.

P1-D: exactly one semantics for the FS window. SPK private retention is current + 2 previous = 3, window 90 days; '2 total / 60 days' is invalid. OPK private is destroyed immediately after successful AEAD; the old DHs_priv is destroyed right after the DH ratchet (only the current pair is kept); MKSKIPPED is TTL/limit bounded. PCS is only after a reply DH ratchet, not instant; SESSION_IDLE_TTL is GC, not an FS boundary. Zeroization is best-effort JS and is stated honestly.

inputs.spk_ttl_field_semantics: rotation interval (legacy field name); private-SPK retention is spk_retain_window_days

expected.zeroization: best_effort (delete IndexedDB record, overwrite raw buffers, drop refs)
expected.test: storage scan after N ratchets/rotations + state-machine test

sections.title: K_storage 50-byte AAD layout, injectivity and pin scope (E7-F2G P1-07/P2-18)

vectors.note: Normative fixed-width 50-byte AAD (docs/E2EE-SPEC.md §2.3.1): owner device UUID (RFC 4122 bytes) || session_id (16-byte protocol id, or 0x16 sentinel) || client_message_id UUID (or 0x16) || record_type u8 || LOCAL_RECORD_VERSION u8 (=1). Fixed AES-256-GCM key/nonce/plaintext; the expected ciphertext||tag must match byte-for-byte. The key is a public KAT value and must never be used by a client.

Absent optional ids are encoded as 16 zero bytes; a present id is never all-zero. buildKStorageAad rejects nil UUIDs and all-zero session/client ids, so the zero sentinel is unambiguous and two different logical scopes cannot produce the same 50-byte AAD.

Normative pin AAD slots (docs/E2EE-SPEC.md §2.3.2, CR1b P2-18). The same 50-byte layout is reused: session_id carries the target device UUID and client_message_id the owner user UUID for pin/key-change; modePin carries the chat UUID and 0x16 for the user slot. record_type separates pin=4, keyChange=5, modePin=6.
